name: Stepper
summary: Shows the steps of a process in order, which are complete, which one is current and which are still to come.
useWhen: A task split into three to seven ordered steps, such as a checkout, an onboarding or a setup
The user needs to see how far they are and what is left
The user may go back to an earlier step, or jump between steps in free mode
avoidWhen: Views of the same content that have no order (use tabs)
Progress of a single running task with a percentage
A process of one or two steps, where a heading is enough
The main navigation of an app

steps.description: One entry per step: title (a short noun), description (one line), invalid, disabled, href, id.

current.description: The index of the current step, from 0. Controlled. Without it the stepper keeps its own, starting at defaultCurrent.

defaultCurrent.description: The first current step when current is not passed.

completed.description: Indexes of the complete steps. Default every step before the furthest step reached, so going back keeps them complete.

mode.description: linear: earlier steps can be reached, a later step only when every step before it is complete. free: any step that is not disabled. The rule lives in packages/shared/src/stepper.ts.

onStepSelect.description: Called when the user picks a step. When it is passed, or a step has href, every step the user may reach, other than the current one, renders its title as a system Button.

orientation.description: Sets data-orientation. A horizontal stepper takes the vertical layout under breakpoint.phone (30rem), so it never scrolls sideways.

size.description: md: a 32px indicator (size.control.sm) and text s. sm: a 24px indicator (size.icon.lg) and text xs.

labels.description: The list name and the hidden state words. Defaults: Steps, current step, complete, has errors, unavailable; under an Arabic Theme الخطوات، الخطوة الحالية، مكتملة، فيها أخطاء، غير متاحة.

aria-label.description: The name of the list. Name the process: Checkout steps.

a11y.role: list (an ol), each step a listitem; a step the user may reach holds a button or a link
a11y.focus: Only steps the user may reach are tab stops, each a system Button with the focus ring from focus.shadow.ring. Static steps and the current step are not focusable.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next step the user may reach
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the previous step the user may reach
keys.Space: Goes to the focused step when it is a button

a11y.announce: The list name, then each step with its position from the list (2 of 4), its title and hidden words: current step, complete, has errors, unavailable. The current step also carries aria-current="step".
notes: Complete shows a check and invalid shows a danger glyph, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The indicator is hidden from assistive tech; the hidden status words carry the state.
The step number is not read from the indicator: the ordered list gives the position.
The connector fill starts at the inline start, so it grows from the right in RTL.
Under forced colors the indicator border takes CanvasText, the current step Highlight, and the connector stays a border.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.
React Native has no current state: the current step says current step in its accessibilityLabel.

en.title: A short noun in sentence case: Account, Address, Payment, Review. Not a verb, not a sentence.
en.description: One line that says what the step asks for: Email and password.
en.count: Three to seven steps. More than seven: group them, or use the vertical form.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الحساب، العنوان، الدفع، المراجعة.
ar.description: One short line in white Saudi dialect.

react.behavior: hand built ol; state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts; reachable steps are system Buttons (asChild for links)
react.note: Motion tab-indicator: the connector fill scales from the start side when a step completes; under reduced motion it swaps at once. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction stepper-travel: a ring on the indicator's ::after, drawn only while it travels, slides from the old current indicator to the new one (internal/indicator.ts, ghost form), the new indicator pops, and the connector fill moves on the soft spring.

angular.behavior: ol[dsStepper] host bindings, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts, reachable steps as button[dsButton] or a[dsButton]
angular.note: onStepSelect is a function input: steps become actions only when it is set, as in React. Step title and description take a string or a TemplateRef. Stepper.css is used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View list with Pressable steps, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
native.note: Vertical on phones; the connector is a View.

styles.studio: Neutral: a complete step is the neutral fill with a check, the current step a bright ring, the filled connector bright on a dim track.
styles.desk: The yellow family: a complete step is the yellow fill with ink, the current step a yellow ring, the filled connector yellow.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Complete told apart from upcoming by color only
mistakes.right: Stepper, which draws a check and says complete in hidden words

mistakes.wrong: A Stepper used as tabs for views with no order
Step titles that are actions: Enter your address
Twelve steps in a horizontal row on a wide screen
mistakes.right: Group the steps, or use orientation vertical

mistakes.wrong: Every step clickable in a process where later steps need earlier data
mistakes.right: mode linear, the default, which opens a later step only when the ones before it are complete
